D23 — 2026-10-04
chose: 2.13: the Stop gate (D10, D11) reads its inputs cheaply; it asks for the same things as before. (1) Rules: the declared index as the session's last hook refreshed it, with no freshness pass over every log at Stop. The bound record's own entries are rebuilt from the fold Stop already holds, so a rule the session logged after its last tool call still bears. (2) Edits: git status runs only when this session ran a command that may write a file. PostToolUse (and PostToolUseFailure) classify each shell command, and a may-write one marks the session in .sofar/.index/wrote/<session>.json. A command made only of test runs and known read-only heads (cat, grep, ls, git status/log/diff/show…, sed without -i), with no output redirection, never marks. Every other command does. A session with commands but no mark skips the spawn. (3) Both engines mirror both.
over: Defaulting the gate off (it carries R4-A, round 4's main ≥50% claim, D9; the orchestrator relayed it stays on). A per-session may-write flag in the fold (checkpoint, fold-parity and edge changes for one boolean). Reimplementing git status from .git/index in-process. Keeping the freshness pass (12 ms of stat at 1,000 records).
because: D18 on i1000-10mb: Stop +23.9% vs rc.4, and the gate alone is +48.9 ms (SOFAR_ENFORCE arm). Profiled: index freshness 11.7–13.4 ms, the git spawn 20.6–26.5 ms. Measured as arms, skipping the spawn saves 14.0 ms and skipping the freshness pass 21.6 ms; both together put Stop at −12.3% vs rc.4 (one run, load rising). Staleness is bounded: other records' rules are as fresh as the session's last tool call, so a new rule there reaches the next Stop. PREDICT: i1000 Stop ≤ +10% vs rc.4 on both fixtures. R4-A unchanged: a session the hooks observed is asked exactly when it was before, except one whose commands were only reads and tests.
